title: The sheaf of a graded module on Proj and the twisting sheaves O(d)
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be an $\mathbf N$-graded commutative ring and $X=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-nagata-affine-proj]; for $f\in S$ homogeneous of positive degree, $D_+(f)\subseteq X$ is its standard open and $\Gamma(D_+(f),\mathcal O_X)=S_{(f)}$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. (1) For a graded $S$-module $M=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}M_n$, the sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules associated to $M$, written $\widetilde M$, is the sheaf $\mathcal F$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (b): $\Gamma(D_+(f),\widetilde M)=M_{(f)}=\{x/f^m: m\ge0,\ x\in M_{m\deg f}\}\subseteq M_f$ as a module over $S_{(f)}$ for every homogeneous $f$ of positive degree, with the restriction maps $\rho_{f,g}:M_{(f)}\to M_{(g)}$ of (a) of that lemma for $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$ (determined up to unique isomorphism compatible with these identifications). (2) For $d\in\mathbf Z$ the shifted graded module $M(d)$ is the $S$-module $M$ with the grading $M(d)_n=M_{d+n}$. The $d$-th twist of the structure sheaf is $\mathcal O_X(d)=\widetilde{S(d)}$ ($S$ graded as an $S$-module with $S_n=0$ for $n<0$). Thus $\Gamma(D_+(f),\mathcal O_X(d))=S(d)_{(f)}=(S_f)_d$, where $(S_f)_d=\{a/f^m\in S_f: m\ge0,\ a\in S_{m\deg f+d}\}$ (the fractions of degree $d$), an $S_{(f)}$-module by multiplication in $S_f$; and for $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$ the restriction $(S_f)_d\to(S_g)_d$ is the restriction of the canonical localization homomorphism $S_f\to S_g$ (which exists because $f$ is invertible in $S_g$). (3) For $d\ge0$ and $s\in S_d$, the global section $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ is the image of $s\in S(d)_0=S_d$ under the map $M_0\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (d) for $M=S(d)$: the unique global section whose restriction to every $D_+(f)$ is $s/1\in(S_f)_d$. (Summed over $d\ge0$ these give the map $S\to\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ of Stacks 01MM.)

source.place: Constructions, Definition 01M6 (label definition-structure-sheaf) (3) for $\widetilde M$; Definition 01MN (label definition-twist) (1) for $\mathcal O_X(n)=\widetilde{S(n)}$; Lemma 01M7 (label lemma-proj-sheaves) (2),(3),(6), the maps (equation-map-global-sections-degree-n) of Section 01MJ and (equation-global-sections) $S\to\bigoplus_n\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X(n))$ of Section 01MM for the sections $s$; Algebra, Sections 00JL (twist $M(n)$) and 00JM ($M_{(f)}$)

proof.text: *$\widetilde M$ is well defined.* For a graded $S$-module $M$, [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (a) gives the $S_{(f)}$-linear restriction maps $\rho_{f,g}:M_{(f)}\to M_{(g)}$ for $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$, $x/f^m\mapsto b^mx/g^{em}$ where $g^e=bf$, independent of the choices and transitive; its clause (b) gives a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal F(D_+(f))=M_{(f)}$ as $S_{(f)}$-modules and restriction maps $\rho_{f,g}$, unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with these identifications. So clause (1) names a sheaf, determined up to unique isomorphism, as in Stacks Definition 01M6 (3) and Lemma 01M7 (2),(3).

source.place: Section 01M3, the paragraph before Definition 01M6 (Sheaves, Lemma extend-off-basis-module); Definition 01M6 (3); Lemma 01M7 (2),(3)

proof.text: *$M(d)$ is a graded $S$-module, and $S(d)_{(f)}=(S_f)_d$.* $M(d)$ has the same underlying $S$-module as $M$ and $M(d)=\bigoplus_nM(d)_n$ with $M(d)_n=M_{d+n}$ (a reindexing of the decomposition of $M$); and $S_e\cdot M(d)_n=S_e M_{d+n}\subseteq M_{d+n+e}=M(d)_{n+e}$. So $M(d)$ is a graded $S$-module (Stacks 00JL). Take $M=S$ (with $S_n=0$ for $n<0$) and $f\in S_k$, $k\ge1$. As $S$-modules $S(d)=S$, so $S(d)_f=S_f$ with its $S_f$-module structure given by multiplication. By the definition of $M_{(f)}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (Stacks 00JM), $S(d)_{(f)}$ is the set of $x/f^m\in S(d)_f=S_f$ with $m\ge0$ and $x\in S(d)_{mk}=S_{mk+d}$: this is exactly $(S_f)_d$ as defined in (2) (empty of nonzero elements for $mk+d<0$, since $S_n=0$ for $n<0$). The $S_{(f)}$-module structure of $M_{(f)}$ is the restriction of the $S_f$-module structure of $M_f$ to the subring $S_{(f)}\subseteq S_f$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], i.e. here multiplication in $S_f$: $(r/f^n)(a/f^m)=ra/f^{n+m}$ with $ra\in S_{(n+m)k+d}$, which lies in $(S_f)_d$ again. Restrictions: for $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$ with $g^e=bf$, $b$ homogeneous, $f\cdot(b/g^e)=1$ in $S_g$, so $f$ is a unit of $S_g$ and the canonical homomorphism $\lambda:S_f\to S_g$ exists, with $\lambda(a/f^m)=a\,(b/g^e)^m=ab^m/g^{em}$; this is the formula of $\rho_{f,g}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (a) for $M=S(d)$. So the restriction $(S_f)_d\to(S_g)_d$ of $\mathcal O_X(d)$ is $\lambda$ restricted to $(S_f)_d$. This is clause (2), Stacks Definition 01MN (1) with Lemma 01M7 (2),(3).

source.place: Section 00JL (twist $M(n)_d=M_{n+d}$), Section 00JM (definition of $S_{(f)}$, $M_{(f)}$); constructions.tex Definition 01MN (1), Lemma 01M7 (2),(3)

proof.text: *The global section $s$ of (3) exists and is unique.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (d) to the graded module $M=S(d)$, $d\ge0$: $M_0=S(d)_0=S_d$, and for $s\in S_d$ the element $s/1\in M_{(f)}$ is, under step 2, $s/f^0\in(S_f)_d$. Clause (d) says these elements are compatible under the $\rho_{f,g}$ and are the restrictions of a unique global section of $\mathcal O_X(d)$; this global section is the $s$ of (3), and $s\mapsto s$ is the $S_0$-linear map $S_d\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ of Stacks Lemma 01M7 (6) (equation (01MJ) map-global-sections-degree-n), summed over $d$ the map (equation-global-sections) of Section 01MM. (Compatibility is visible directly: with $m=0$, $\rho_{f,g}(s/1)=b^0s/g^0=s/1$; uniqueness and existence then also follow from the sheaf property of $\mathcal O_X(d)$ on the cover of $X$ by the $D_+(f)$, which is how Stacks argues in the proof of 01M7 (6); here the clause (d) of the existence lemma is cited.)
